affectedRule: Fast Spell activation cost and target-selection transaction

castle.observation: Fast Spell follows the ordinary learned-spell source path. Castle rejects exact-cost activation through its greater-than-or-equal check and prepays learned spell points before cancellable target selection. In combat, an abort costs three movement and refunds about two thirds of learned spell points, spends no attack units, and decrements spellsofar only for learned casts. Successful targeting spends twelve movement and two half-attacks. Scroll consumption occurs at getscroll; combat item charges are committed at their source branch. These source observations do not constitute native Castle UI proof.

playerFacingProblem: Fast Spell can reject a legal exact-cost cast, while deferring every source payment until confirmation omits Castle combat commitment and abort costs.
chosenBehavior: Fast Spell shares the typed staged-cast workflow with the spellbook. Learned spells prepay before target selection and use Castle abort movement and 66-percent refund behavior; item charges and scroll slots are consumed before aiming and remain spent on abort. Exact-cost activation is permitted. Automatic and AI casts remain one-phase.
legacyQuirk: Manual combat abort costs three movement without spending attacks. Learned spells retain the lifetime-cast increment and refund 66 percent of the paid SP, rounded down, while releasing the turn spell count. Consumed item charges and scroll slots are not restored.
